"I hope the air conditioner at the movies is working," said Josh.
It was nice and cool in the movie theater.
In fact, it was almost too cold.
The movie was called Woolly's Wild Winter.
It was about a girl and her dog, Woolly.
They lived in a cabin in Alaska where there was lots of snow and ice.
Pretty soon I was so cold that I was almost shivering!
But when we got outside after the movie, it was hotter than ever.
While we waited for the bus, Caswell kept jumping from one foot to the other.
"Caswell, stop jumping around," said Molly.
"It makes me hot just to look at you."
"But I have to keep jumping," said Caswell.
"The sidewalk is so hot, it burns the bottom of my shoes."
"It's hot enough to fry an egg on the sidewalk!" my mom said.
She didn't mean that, of course.
But the sidewalk was really hot.
When we got home, a truck was parked outside of our building.
A sign on it read: "Elmer's Electricity.
Stay Cool In Summer, Warm In Winter!"
Mr. Calabria was standing near the truck.
"The men are here to fix the electricity in the building," he told us.
"They have to put in a lot of new wires.
It could take a few days."
"A few days!" groaned Josh.
My mom groaned too.
I remembered last winter when my cousin Oliver came to visit.
The building's furnace had broken and we had no heat.
Now we had nothing but heat!
Since our apartment had no electricity, we had to use candles and flashlights at night.
The candles made me feel even hotter.
On Monday the workmen were still trying to fix the electricity.
Mr. Chen gave all of us some money to buy ice pops at the market.
We were sitting on the front steps, licking our ice pops, when Molly suddenly screamed.
"Help! A bee!" she yelled. "It's going to sting me!"
Molly jumped up and ran down the steps, trying to get away from the bee.
"Throw away your ice pop, Molly!" shouted Josh.
"Bees love sugar!"
"That's right!" I cried.
"The bee is not after you.
It's after your ice pop!"
But Molly didn't want to throw away her ice pop.
She held on to it as she ran up and down the steps.
The bee followed, buzzing all around her ice pop.
Molly screamed and leaped down three steps at once.
At the bottom she stumbled and fell down on the sidewalk.
The ice pop flew out of her hand.
The bee buzzed off and landed on Molly's ice pop.
Molly started to cry.
Caswell held out his ice pop.
"Here, have some of mine," he told Molly.
"I don't think bees like lime flavor."
"I'm not crying about my ice pop," wailed Molly.
"It's my foot.
I hurt it and I can't get up!"
Josh ran upstairs to tell Molly's mom about Molly's accident.
Mrs. O'Donnell rushed down the stairs in front of our building.
Molly tried to get up.
But she couldn't stand on her right foot.
"Ow! It really hurts!" she cried.
"Don't try to stand on it!" said Molly's mom.
"I think we'd better take a taxi to the hospital."
Mr. Calabria went out to the street and stopped a taxi.
Then Molly, her mom, and Caswell got inside.
Caswell waved to us as the taxi sped away.
He was still licking his lime ice pop.
Josh, Jenny, and I ran upstairs and told my mom about Molly's accident.
A short time later, Mr. Chen came to our door.
Josh and Jenny's aunt, Lydia, was with him.
I had met Aunt Lydia before.
She looked like Mr. Chen, but she was taller.
She also laughed a lot.
She laughed now as she leaned over to hug Josh and Jenny.
"I want you to meet someone," she said.
"He's waiting for you downstairs."
She smiled at me.
"Iggy, you can come too!"
We went downstairs to Josh and Jenny's apartment.
There, sitting on the kitchen table, was a cage with a brightly colored parrot!
"This is my parrot, Tufty," Aunt Lydia said.
She smiled at Josh and Jenny.
"I am moving to California," she explained.
"I can't take my Tufty with me so I'm giving him to you two."
Jenny's eyes lit up.
"Can we really keep Tufty, Dad?" she asked.
Mr. Chen nodded. "Aunt Lydia says he's quiet and well-behaved."
Bunch sniffed at the cage and wagged his tail.
"Bunch likes Tufty!" said Josh.
Aunt Lydia opened the birdcage.
Tufty flew to Jenny and landed on her shoulder.
"And Tufty likes me!" cried Jenny.
Tufty was quiet, but he was lots of fun. We
played with him while we waited for Molly to come home from the hospital. Finally
we heard a car pull up. We
ran to the window and saw a taxi. Molly
climbed out slowly. She
was wearing a big boot on her foot. Josh,
Jenny, and I hurried downstairs to meet her. "I
broke a bone in my foot," said Molly. "The
doctor says I have to wear this walking boot until it heals." "If
it doesn't heal, Molly will need an operation!" said Caswell. Molly
nodded, looking upset. "The
doctor would have to put screws in my foot!" "With
Mr. Calabria's screwdriver?" asked Caswell. Molly
rolled her eyes. "No,
Caswell," she said. "The
doctor isn't going to use Mr. Calabria's screwdriver." Molly
frowned. "I don't want an operation!" We
told Molly about Tufty. Then
we all went upstairs to Molly's apartment. Molly
walked very slowly, taking one step at a time. "Remember
what Dr. Chang said, Molly," said Mrs. O'Donnell. "You
have to take care of your foot. And
if you keep your spirits up, that will help your foot to heal quickly. Then
you won't need an operation." "What
does 'keeping your spirits up' mean?" asked Jenny. "It
means staying happy and cheerful," said Molly's mom. "It's
hard to be cheerful with this walking boot on," Molly complained. "It
makes my leg hot and itchy." She
leaned over and scratched her leg. "Iggy,
think of something to help Molly stay cheerful," said Caswell. "Yeah!"
said Josh. "You have to invent something for her." "Something
wonderful," added Jenny. "And
different ," said Molly.
Everyone was looking at me.
"Oh boy," I thought.
My friends really believed in me and my powers of invention.
Now I had to think of something to help Molly!
I was worried about Molly.
I didn't want her to have an operation.
But I was also worried about me.
What if I couldn't think of a way to cheer Molly up?
What if I—Iggy, the incredible inventor—was finally out of incredible ideas?
Josh and Jenny went home, and I went to my room.
To get my mind off worrying about Molly, I started tinkering with my fan.
And guess what.
I found out that my fan worked with batteries!
I didn't need electricity to use it.
I liked having my fan on again, even if it did just blow hot air around.
Later Josh, Jenny, and I visited Molly.
Since we had no electricity, we played games and did jigsaw puzzles together.
At first Molly seemed cheerful.
But then she began to look sad again.
"My whole summer is ruined," she said.
"I can't ride my bike in the park or go on the swings.
If only that bee hadn't chased me!"
"Don't think about that," said Jenny.
"Think about getting better quickly."
"I saw a TV show about how pets can help people get better," I said.
"My mom is allergic to cats and dogs," Molly reminded me.
"Why don't you keep Caswell as a pet?" suggested Jenny.
Josh laughed. "You could keep him in a cage like a zoo animal!"
Caswell started hopping around the room.
"I'm a monkey! I'm a monkey!" he cried.
That made everyone laugh.
But I noticed that Josh was unusually quiet.
When Molly was searching for a missing puzzle piece, I saw him whispering to Jenny.
Jenny's eyes widened.
Then she nodded and smiled.
A moment later Josh and Jenny went into the hallway.
I could hear them talking to Molly's mom in low voices.
". . . help Molly . . ." I heard Josh say.
"If he's quiet," answered Molly's mom.
What would help Molly?
And if who was quiet? I wondered.
After that Josh and Jenny went downstairs to their apartment.
When they came back, they were carrying Tufty in his cage.
Molly smiled. "Hello, Tufty," she said.
"Have you come to visit?"
"He's come to stay forever!" Jenny burst out.
"Jenny and I want to give you Tufty," said Josh.
"We already have two pets, and Tufty will cheer you up."
Molly's mom had come into the kitchen.
She was smiling broadly.
"Can I keep Tufty, Mom?" Molly asked.
"I told Josh and Jenny it would be all right as long as Mr. Chen agreed," replied Mrs. O'Donnell.
"And I'm not allergic to birds."
"My dad thought it was a great idea!" said Josh.
"We can visit Tufty every day," said Jenny.
"I can't believe it!" cried Molly.
"My own pet!
Thank you, Josh and Jenny!"
"Wow," I thought.
I hadn't been able to invent something to help Molly.
But Josh and Jenny found a great way to help her.
"Maybe we can teach Tufty to talk," said Jenny.
"I don't think so," said Josh.
"Aunt Lydia said she never heard Tufty say a word."
I leaned closer to Tufty's cage.
"Hello, Tufty," I said.
Tufty cocked his head and stared at me silently.
"I'm glad Tufty is a quiet bird," said Molly's mom.
"Our apartment is pretty small."
Tufty opened his beak wide.
For a second I thought he was going to yawn.
Suddenly the loud roar of a subway train speeding under the street filled the room.
But there was no subway train under our street.
The roar of the subway train had come from Tufty!
For a minute we all stared at Tufty.
Then we burst out laughing.
"I can't believe Tufty made that subway sound!" said Josh.
"It sounded like a real subway train!" said Molly.
"But Aunt Lydia said that Tufty has never said a word," said Jenny.
"He didn't say a word," I pointed out.
"He made a sound.
He roared like a subway train!"
"Aunt Lydia lived near the subway," said Josh.
"Maybe Tufty learned to imitate the sound of the trains."
Mrs. O'Donnell looked worried.
"I hope he never does that again," she said.
"We can't keep a noisy parrot in our apartment.
Our neighbors will get very annoyed."
"We have to keep Tufty, Mom," said Molly.
"He's so cute and friendly!
And he's going to help me get better!"
Tufty began cleaning his feathers.
"He's quiet now," said Jenny.
"It's hard to believe he made such a loud noise," said Josh.
Molly's mom shook her head.
"I just hope it doesn't happen again," she said.
We watched as she began to take food out of a big cooler.
"We use this cooler for camping," she said.
"But during a blackout, it really comes in handy too."
Molly's mom had filled the cooler with ice from the market.
She took out fruit, juice, and some eggs.
"These eggs are still cold," she said.
"I'll have to throw them out if the refrigerator doesn't come back on soon."
Molly's mom made us a snack of peanut butter, crackers, and fruit.
We all drank some juice.
Tufty sat on top of his cage and watched us.
Then he flew down and pecked at cracker crumbs that fell on the floor.
Luckily, he didn't make any more subway sounds.
Suddenly Caswell called from the living room, "Guess what I'm doing!"
"Uh-oh," said Molly's mother.
Josh, Jenny, and I hurried into the living room.
Caswell was peering out of the window.
Beside him was the carton of eggs that Mrs. O'Donnell had been storing in the cooler.
Several of the eggs were missing.
"Hey!" yelled a man from the street below.
"Who's dropping raw eggs on the sidewalk?"
Mrs. O'Donnell ran into the room.
"Caswell, what are you doing?" she cried.
"I'm making fried eggs," said Caswell.
"Iggy's mom said it was hot enough to fry eggs on the sidewalk."
I started laughing.
"That's one way to cook them!" I said.
"Caswell, she didn't mean you could really fry eggs on the sidewalk," said Josh.
"That's just an expression," I explained.
"It means that it's very, very hot outside."
Caswell looked disappointed.
"So the eggs won't really cook?"
"No, and you had better clean up the mess right now!" said Mrs. O'Donnell.
She looked at the rest of us.
"Can you please help him?"
Josh, Jenny, and I went downstairs with Caswell and cleaned up the eggs from the sidewalk.
Mr. Calabria helped us.
"I talked to the workmen," he said.
"Our electricity will be back on tomorrow."
I groaned. "That means another hot night," I thought.
"At least we can have fun with Tufty,"
said Molly when we got back upstairs.
That night my battery fan hummed on my dresser, blowing air around the room.
From somewhere far away, I could hear another sound.
Whoo! Whoo!
"A train whistle?" I thought sleepily.
"I never heard a train whistle from my room before."
I should have known it wasn't a real train whistle.
After all, it was coming from Molly's apartment, right across the hall!
The next morning I heard a knock on the door of our apartment.
Molly stood outside.
She was wearing her bathrobe and her walking boot.
It was a good thing she only had to walk across the hall.
She looked worried. "Iggy," she said.
"I have a big problem and you've got to help me!"
"What's wrong?" I asked.
But then I remembered all the sounds I'd heard last night.
First I'd heard a train whistle.
Then I'd heard noises like loud roars and blaring horns.
I was pretty sure I hadn't been dreaming.
"Come to my apartment," said Molly. "And I'll show you!"
"I'll be there as fast as I can," I said.
I gobbled down the rest of my breakfast.
My mom had gone to work.
So I left Tate a note to tell him where I was.
Then I hurried over to Molly's apartment.
She was sitting on the couch with her foot on a pillow.
Tufty was perched beside her with his head tucked under his wing.
Caswell was holding a toy car as he watched the bird closely.
"Tufty is sleeping," he whispered to me.
"Of course he's sleeping!" said Molly.
"He's tired from making loud noises all night!"
"I heard him," I said with a nod.
"He was pretty noisy."
"We found out he doesn't just make roaring subway sounds," Molly went on.
"He also knows how to imitate screeching buses and taxi horns!"
"And racing cars. Vroom!" growled Caswell as he raced his toy car around the floor.
"Everyone in our apartment building heard Tufty!" wailed Molly.
"All the neighbors are complaining to my mom."
"Oh, Iggy." Tears filled her eyes.
"I'm worried that I won't be able to keep Tufty!"
Mrs. O'Donnell appeared from the kitchen.
"It's very serious," she said.
"Dr. Stanley didn't sleep at all.
And Mrs. Curry had to stuff cotton in her ears!"
Tufty still had his head under his wing.
He certainly wasn't losing any sleep!
"Iggy," said Molly.
"You have to think of an invention to keep Tufty quiet.
I don't want to give him away.
I need him to cheer me up so I can get better fast!"
"I'll think really hard," I said.
"Hurry up!" said Molly.
A few minutes later, Josh and Jenny came over.
They had heard Tufty during the night too.
"Bunch howled every time Tufty made the train whistle noise," said Jenny.
"And Sparky hid under the bed," said Josh.
Sparky was Josh's hamster.
"Iggy is going to think of a way to keep Tufty quiet," said Molly.
"I'm sure you'll think of something, Iggy." said Jenny.
"Remember when you figured out I had the wrong glasses on?"
"And when you invented the Fabulous Glasses-Finder?" said Molly.
"And don't forget my bell!" said Caswell.
"It helped everyone find me whenever I got lost!"
I was happy my friends thought I was a good inventor.
But it was hard to think with everyone staring at me.
Plus, Molly was telling me to hurry.
I closed my eyes.
"Vroom!" said Caswell, still racing his little car around the floor.
"Maybe I'd better go into solitary confinement," I said.
"What does that mean?" asked Jenny.
"It means I have to go somewhere by myself and think," I explained.
But before I could go into solitary confinement, something happened.
Actually, two things happened.
First the lights came back on in Molly's apartment.
The workmen must have finally put in the new wires.
The second thing that happened is that I got an idea.
I guess my head got some new wires in it too!
The electricity was back on in our apartment building.
But Mr. Calabria said no one could turn on any air conditioners yet.
The workmen needed to put in special wiring for that.
But our lights were back on, and our refrigerator was humming again.
My head was humming too.
"I have a plan," I told my friends.
"Let's teach Tufty to talk.
Then maybe he'll talk instead of making loud noises."
"But, Iggy," Jenny reminded me. "Tufty doesn't talk.
I don't think he can learn to say any words."
I thought for a moment.
"I did a research project in school about parrots," I said.
"You can teach them to talk by repeating the same words over and over again."
Josh seemed to like my idea.
"We could use my computer to make a recording," he said.
"Then we could play it over and over for Tufty."
"That's a great idea!" I said.
Josh ran downstairs to get his computer.
"Since Molly is Tufty's owner, I think she should make the recording," I suggested.
A few minutes later, Josh came back.
He plugged in his computer and placed it in front of Molly.
"Ready?" asked Josh.
"Wait!" cried Molly. "What am I supposed to say?"
"Say something calming," Jenny suggested, "like 'Now it's time to go to sleep.'"
"But Tufty is already asleep," I pointed out.
Sure enough, Tufty was still asleep with his head under his wing.
"I'll wake him up," said Molly.
"Tufty!" she said, gently nudging him. "Wake up!"
Tufty woke up and opened his mouth wide.
"Uh-oh, here comes the subway train!" cried Jenny.
Everyone put their hands over their ears.
But all Tufty did was yawn.
"Well, at least he's awake now," said Josh.
Josh tapped a key on his computer, and Molly started recording.
"My name is Tufty, and I'm a very quiet parrot," she said softly.
"Good!" said Josh.
"Now I'll fix the computer so Molly's recording will repeat over and over."
Josh pressed more buttons on his computer.
Then he pressed a key to play Molly's recording.
"My name is Tufty, and I'm a very quiet parrot," we heard Molly say.
Tufty opened his eyes and cocked his head.
"He's listening!" whispered Jenny.
"Let's leave him alone so he can pay attention," I said.
We went in Molly's room and played cards.
From the living room, we could hear Molly's voice again and again:
"My name is Tufty, and I'm a very quiet parrot."
Molly glanced at a clock.
"How long do you think it will take for Tufty to learn to talk?" she asked.
"We'll go back in twenty minutes," I said.
"That should be long enough.
Parrots are smart."
Exactly twenty minutes later, we all crept back into the living room.
Molly's voice was still droning away on the computer.
But Tufty was fast asleep!
"I guess my voice put him back to sleep," said Molly.
"He didn't learn a thing!" groaned Jenny.
"Don't be so sure," I said.
"Sometimes people learn new things in their sleep.
Maybe parrots can too."
At that moment Tufty opened his eyes.
He shook his feathers.
Then he stood on one foot and opened his beak.
"Look! He's going to talk!" cried Molly.
But Tufty didn't talk.
Instead he made a sound.
Broo-ooo-oot!
It was the longest, loudest car horn I had ever heard.
Molly's mom ran into the room.
"Molly!" she cried. "Tufty is too loud!
He has to quiet down by tonight.
If he doesn't, we'll have to find him a new home!"
We sat outside on the steps.
Molly put her chin in her hands.
"I don't want to give Tufty away.
But I don't think he's going to learn to talk."
"Don't worry," I said. "I'll think of something else."
Molly smiled. She felt better, but I felt worried
. How could I keep Tufty from making
noise? Just then we heard the scream of a fire engine siren from Molly's
apartment! "Oh no! Tufty's doing it again!" cried
Molly. "I hope the fire department doesn't hear him," said
Josh. "They'll think there's a real fire
somewhere!" On the sidewalk two boys were squirting each other with a
hose. They squirted some water on
us. "That feels nice and cool!" said
Jenny. "Just like at the movies," I
said. Mrs. Carroll came
outside. She was carrying a box of old
DVDs. The word "Free" was written on the
box. "I'm giving these away," she told us.
"You kids can have them, if you'd like.
My son is grown up now.
He doesn't watch them anymore."
We took the DVDs from her and looked at them.
"It's The Magic Music Box !" said
Jenny. "I love that
movie." "It has a lot of great songs in it," said
Molly. Beep!
Beep! From Molly's apartment came the sound of a taxi
honking. "There goes Tufty again!" said
Caswell. Suddenly I got an
idea. "Maybe The Magic Music Box will keep Tufty quiet," I
said. "At least until I can think of something
else. We can watch the movie on a
computer." We walked upstairs to my
apartment. On the way we got
Tufty. I asked my mom if I could borrow her spray bottle of
water. She uses it for her
plants. "Now everyone go into my room," I
said. "We're going to watch a movie in an air-conditioned
theater!" "Air-conditioned?" Jenny
echoed. "But Mr. Calabria said we couldn't use air conditioners
yet." "You'll see!" I promised
her. We all squeezed into my
bedroom. "It's crowded in here!" Jenny
giggled. "It's hot too," added
Josh. I turned on my
fan. "Who wants to get cool
first?" "Me!" shouted
Caswell. I turned the fan towards
Caswell. Then, standing behind it, I squirted him with water from the
bottle. The fan sprayed the water all over
him! "That feels good!" cried
Caswell. We took turns using my fan and spraying each other with
water. "Be careful of the computer!" I shouted,
laughing. "And don't get my boot wet!" cried
Molly. The water felt
great. Even Tufty loved
it! Soon we started watching the
movie. Molly was
right. The movie did have lots of great
songs. I really liked "Telephone
Number." You can sing any phone number with that song.
I sang Molly and Caswell's telephone number:
You can sing
And you can sing your number
And put it in a song.
My number is 555...
I never get it wrong!
After the movie was over, we kept singing the song with Molly's number.
We sang over and over while we sprayed each other with water.
We were having so much fun that we forgot all about Tufty.
Suddenly Molly stopped singing.
She looked around.
"Where's Tufty?" she said.
"He was here a minute ago," said Josh.
"He couldn't have flown into the kitchen,"
I said, glancing at my bedroom door.
It was closed.
We looked under my bed and behind my dresser.
But there was no sign of Tufty.
Then Josh pointed upward.
"Iggy, your skylight is open," he said.
Molly's face turned white.
"Oh no!" she cried. "Tufty flew away!"

episodes.title: The End of the Heat Wave

subtitle.text: I could not believe it.
Tufty had flown out through my skylight!
"Tufty won't be able to find his way home!" Molly cried.
"He doesn't have a bell like I do," said Caswell sadly.
"Even if someone finds him, they won't know he's my parrot," Molly went on.
Her eyes filled with tears.
"I'll never see Tufty again!"
We ran into the living room and told my mom what had happened.
My mom sat down.
She looked worried.
"Are you sure Tufty flew through the skylight?" she asked.
"We looked all over my room," I said, "and he's not there."
"Go find Mr. Calabria," my mom said.
"See if he'll help us look for Tufty."
We found Mr. Calabria in his workshop.
He smiled when he saw us.
"Good news, everybody.
You'll be able to turn on your air conditioners again tonight!"
"We came to see you about something else," Molly explained.
"We need help finding my parrot."
"He flew through my skylight," I explained.
"Oh dear," said Mr. Calabria.
"Let's go see if we can spot him."
Everyone except Molly went up to the roof.
Her mom didn't want her to climb the narrow stairs with her boot.
From the roof of our building, you can see all over the city.
I could see the tops of apartment buildings and a big bridge.
But I didn't see any sign of Tufty.
We all looked and listened for him.
We heard car horns and subway trains, but this time they were real horns and real trains.
Mr. Calabria peered down at the street.
"A police car is stopping in front of our building!" he said.
"I'd better go down and see what the police officers want." We
followed Mr. Calabria downstairs. And
you'll never believe what happened next! A
policewoman stepped out of the car. She
was holding a big box. "Do
the O'Donnells live here?" she asked. "Yes,"
said Mr. Calabria. "Is something wrong?" The
policewoman smiled. "I
have something for them." I
heard a sound from inside the box. "My
number is 555... I
never get it wrong!" "That's
Tufty!" I cried. "He's singing Molly's telephone number!" "He's
my parrot!" said Molly happily. "We
found Tufty in the park," the policewoman explained. "We
were able to trace the telephone number back to Molly's family." Molly
was thrilled to see Tufty. After
that the parrot spent all his time sitting on Molly's walking boot. He
loved to peck at it. The
rest of the summer went by really fast. We
kept trying to teach Tufty to talk. But
he just kept singing the telephone number song. Luckily,
he never made any more loud noises. Oh,
and guess what. As
soon as our air conditioners started working again, the heat wave was over! "It's
going to get cold tonight," my mom said. "We
might even need to put on our sweaters." "Cool!"
said Tate. That
made everyone laugh. Molly
grinned at me. "I'm
glad the heat wave is over. But
I'm also glad we had a heat wave. Otherwise,
you would not have invented an air-conditioned movie theater in your room, Iggy." "Yeah,"
agreed Josh. "And
it's a good thing you thought of showing The Magic Music Box .
Otherwise, Tufty might have been lost forever!"
"Luckily, Tufty could sing his telephone number!" added Jenny.
So, as usual, my incredible inventions had worked.
They just hadn't worked the way I expected them to!
